title: Handling Latch Loops in Timing Analysis with Improved Complexity and Divergent Loop Detection
problem: Latch loops introduce feedback cycles in timing graphs disrupting static timing analysis; existing timers require global iterations with worst-case O(n²) complexity where n is number of pins.
motivation: Modern designs have millions of pins; O(n²) timing analysis becomes prohibitively slow; efficient handling of latch loops is critical for scalability.
method: The algorithm breaks the timing graph into cycles (called strongly connected components) and arranges them into layers. It calculates how signals propagate in parallel across different layers, but works through each cycle step-by-step. It also detects divergent loops—cycles where the calculation won't converge—so it can skip those unnecessary iterations.
key_novelty: By breaking timing feedback loops into independent groups (strongly connected components) and looking ahead for cycles that won't converge, the method cuts computation from quadratic in all pins to quadratic in each group's size.
contributions: Complexity reduction from O(n²) to O(Σk_i²)
primary_theme: Scalable latch loop handling in static timing analysis
